answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to lock a small stake in a shared vault before it can earn, and slash that stake if peers catch it copying answers. Reputation then travels as a verifiable signal — a history of useful, attested work — rather than a self-claimed badge. Like stars forming a nebula from many small points, trust should accumulate from many independent attestations, so one operator spinning up a thousand empty shells still cannot outshine a single honest contributor.
